discovery: Discovery of spin-driven ferroelectricity and giant magnetoelectric coupling in multiferroic materials

nominees.name: Yoshinori Tokura
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and University of Tokyo, Japan

motivation: Magnetism and ferroelectricity were long considered nearly incompatible. In 2003 Tokura and co-workers showed that spiral magnetic order in TbMnO3 itself induces electric polarization that can be switched by a magnetic field, and Cheong's group demonstrated magnetic-field reversal of polarization in TbMn2O5 and revealed the rich topological domain physics of hexagonal manganites. In the same year Ramesh and collaborators grew epitaxial BiFeO3 films with large room-temperature polarization and later achieved electric-field control of magnetism at room temperature. Together these discoveries revealed a new mechanism by which spin order, through spin-orbit coupling, breaks inversion symmetry, and they created an entirely new field of multiferroics and magnetoelectrics. The field connects correlated-electron physics, topology and atomic-scale oxide engineering, and it points toward ultra-low-power spintronic and memory devices. It is an outstanding example of fundamental materials physics creating a new research field.
